nodes.label: A 27-year-old woman presented with elevated hepatobiliary enzymes
The patient occasionally drank alcohol and was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride
The patient had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease
After stopping alcohol and axitinib, the patient's hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged
Physical examination showed no specific findings
Laboratory tests show ALP 1028 U/L and GGT 257 U/L
Ultrasound shows rough uneven liver parenchyma and an irregular isoechoic area from the porta hepatis to the right dorsal side
The patient may have an immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy such as primary biliary cholangitis
The patient may have extrahepatic/perihilar biliary obstruction
Immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy (e.g., primary biliary cholangitis)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to metastatic malignancy (e.g., renal cell carcinoma metastasis)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (Klatskin tumor)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to benign inflammatory stricture (e.g., primary sclerosing cholangitis or IgG4-related disease)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to choledocholithiasis/Mirizzi syndrome
Liver biopsy reveals PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule with destruction of interlobular bile ducts
Immunohistochemical staining is positive for PAX8, a marker consistent with renal cell carcinoma
Contrast-enhanced CT/MRI show enhancement patterns corresponding to the hilar irregular isoechoic region
Axitinib is a targeted therapeutic agent primarily used for renal cell carcinoma
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to metastatic renal cell carcinoma
